searchText: What link did you find this bug bounty program at? I would also be very suspicious of anyone asking for KYC docs to submit a bug report. Though, I do have a vague memory of being angry at EF for doing unnecessary KYC on something before, maybe it was the bug bounty program. The KYC is for payment, they already accepted the report. The bug submission is through https://ethereum.org/bug-bounty/ that lead to this form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSd28dv9jU4lqC2GK_Vbv2ev5dJ0Tp4K3CF_mSZZB6Ljyb7_QQ/viewform. The report I submitted is actually reflected in changes recently made to Geth. I just want to make sure the people reaching out are legit, because the first email I got from "legal" about KYC was from a kissflow email address. Which seemed odd. Hey <@1421575689509015562>, I'm part of the protocol security team at the EF, but not really working with the bug bounty program. I know for a fact that we do KYC before payment. The form you shared looks correct/legit. <@861807242156572722> (co-leading the program) can confirm. And "kissflow" is a service we use internally 😅 ok, thank you for the update! If you’re talking through bounty@ethereum.org it’s legit. I’m not the one managing your payout but if you’d like I can look it up and ack through the bounty email that it’s legitimate. I have no reason to believe it isn’t legitimate, but I cant be certain without looking it up. If you let me know the alias you used for the form I can find you through that. hi, I went through with the KYC after hearing from jtraglia, but thank you for the offer!
